facts.heading: Patient is nervous about therapy
facts.content: Tomas is quite nervous about attending therapy.
facts.evidence: I am quite nervous, if I am to be honest.

facts.heading: Wife suggested seeking therapy
facts.content: Tomas's wife suggested he seek therapy because things 'can't go on like this'.
facts.evidence: My wife. She says it can't go on like this.

facts.heading: Compulsive checking behavior
facts.content: Tomas checks if he locked the door and turned off the stove thirty times a night.
facts.evidence: Thirty times a night I check if I locked the door and turned off the stove,

facts.heading: Time taken to leave apartment
facts.content: It takes Tomas an hour to leave the apartment.
facts.evidence: it takes me an hour to leave the apartment.

facts.heading: Checking routine details
facts.content: Tomas's routine involves locking the door, going to the elevator, returning, pulling the handle, checking the stove knobs separately, and checking the door again.
facts.evidence: I lock the door, I go to the elevator, I come back and pull the handle. Then I check the stove, every knob separately. Then the door again.

facts.heading: Relief followed by intrusive thought
facts.content: After checking, Tomas feels relieved temporarily, but then an image comes to his head that he didn't do it properly, requiring him to check again.
facts.evidence: I feel relieved for a while. And then an image comes into my head that I didn't do it properly,

facts.heading: Intrusive image of fire
facts.content: Tomas sees a clear image of the apartment on fire when he doubts his actions.
facts.evidence: The apartment on fire. I see it clearly, like a film.

facts.heading: Frequency of intrusive images
facts.content: The intrusive images happen every day, worst in the evening and morning.
facts.evidence: Every day. It's the worst in the evening when we go out or go to sleep. In the morning too.

facts.heading: Fire incident started two years ago
facts.content: The issue started two years ago after the neighbors' house caught fire and they had to evacuate.
facts.evidence: It started two years ago when the neighbors' house caught fire and we had to evacuate.

facts.heading: Traumatic fire event details
facts.content: The fire happened at night, waking Tomas with smoke in the hallway and screaming.
facts.evidence: It was at night. The alarm woke me up. There was smoke in the hallway and people were screaming.

facts.heading: Feeling of responsibility for fire
facts.content: Since the fire, Tomas feels he can cause it, and if he doesn't control something, it will happen and he will be to blame.
facts.evidence: Since then I have the feeling that I can cause it. That if I don't control something, it will happen and I will be to blame.

facts.heading: Physical symptoms of anxiety
facts.content: When he doesn't want to perform the checks, anxiety causes heart issues, sweating, shaking hands, and stomach sickness.
facts.evidence: Heart, sweat. My hands shake and I feel sick in my stomach.

facts.heading: Wife is aware of the issue
facts.content: Tomas's wife, Barbora, knows about the issue.
facts.evidence: Barbora. My wife.

facts.heading: Wife's perception of the issue
facts.content: Barbora initially thought it was a habit, but now she sees it is more serious.
facts.evidence: At first she took it as a habit, now she sees that it's more.

facts.heading: Wife's patience is exhausting
facts.content: Tomas observes that his wife's patience is being exhausted by the situation.
facts.evidence: I see that it is exhausting her.

facts.heading: Late arrival at cinema
facts.content: Tomas and Barbora arrived at the cinema forty minutes late yesterday.
facts.evidence: Yesterday we arrived at the cinema forty minutes later.

facts.heading: Wife waited for check
facts.content: Barbora waited outside for Tomas to return and check the stove for the third time.
facts.evidence: She waited outside for me to return and check the stove for the third time.

facts.heading: Felt shame like a child
facts.content: Tomas felt shame, describing himself as a child who cannot leave the house.
facts.evidence: Shame. I felt like a child who can't leave the house.

facts.heading: Works as electrician in Olomouc
facts.content: Tomas works as an electrician in Olomouc, performing wiring in apartments and houses.
facts.evidence: I work as an electrician in Olomouc. I do wiring in apartments and sometimes in houses.

facts.heading: Checks work due to fear of error
facts.content: Tomas checks his work because he fears making a mistake, like connecting a wire incorrectly and causing something to burn.
facts.evidence: I'm afraid that because of my head I will make a mistake once.

facts.heading: Checks work after every job
facts.content: Tomas checks his work after every job, sometimes returning the next day just to look.
facts.evidence: after every job I go back and check.

facts.heading: Colleagues call him a pedant
facts.content: Tomas's colleagues think he is a pedant.
facts.evidence: They think I'm a pedant.

facts.heading: Boss sees him as careful
facts.content: Tomas's boss considers him the most careful in the company.
facts.evidence: The boss tells me I'm the most careful in the company,

facts.heading: Checking adds one hour daily
facts.content: Tomas's checking habits add one hour of work to him every day in the last few months.
facts.evidence: In the last few months, it adds an hour of work to me every day.

facts.heading: Handed over jobs due to time
facts.content: Tomas has given up a few jobs to a colleague because he lacked time.
facts.evidence: I have already handed over a few jobs to a colleague because I didn't have time.

facts.heading: Fears losing job now
facts.content: Tomas is afraid of losing his job, especially now.
facts.evidence: I'm afraid I'll lose my job. Especially now.

facts.heading: Barbora is four months pregnant
facts.content: Barbora is four months pregnant.
facts.evidence: Barbora is four months pregnant.

facts.heading: Waited three years for pregnancy
facts.content: Tomas and Barbora waited three years for the pregnancy.
facts.evidence: We waited for it for three years.

facts.heading: Has intrusive thoughts of harming
facts.content: Tomas has thoughts that he might harm Barbora and the baby.
facts.evidence: That I will harm her and the baby.

facts.heading: Thoughts occur during daily activities
facts.content: Tomas fears the thoughts might happen on their own while cutting bread or standing by the stairs.
facts.evidence: maybe when I'm cutting bread or standing by the stairs.

facts.heading: Never told Barbora about thoughts
facts.content: Tomas has never told Barbora about these thoughts.
facts.evidence: I've never told anyone about it, not even Barbora.

facts.heading: Leaves room or checks to stop thoughts
facts.content: When the thoughts appear, Tomas either leaves the room or goes back to check something to make it stop.
facts.evidence: I leave the room. Or I go back and check something to make it stop.

facts.heading: Sleeps terribly, checks stove
facts.content: Tomas sleeps terribly and wakes up twice at night to check the stove, even if it's off.
facts.evidence: I wake up twice at night and check the stove, even if there is nothing on it.

facts.heading: Walks with Barbora twice weekly
facts.content: Tomas goes for walks with Barbora twice a week.
facts.evidence: Walks twice a week,

facts.heading: Fixing things keeps him busy
facts.content: Fixing things at home keeps Tomas busy.
facts.evidence: Or when I fix something at home, it keeps me busy.

facts.heading: Goal to leave apartment
facts.content: Tomas has a goal to leave the apartment in five minutes.
facts.evidence: To leave the apartment in five minutes.

facts.heading: Goal regarding child
facts.content: Tomas has a goal to look forward to a child without certain thoughts.
facts.evidence: And to look forward to a child without those thoughts.

facts.heading: Fear of exposure therapy
facts.content: Tomas was afraid of therapy where a person is gradually exposed to what they are afraid of.
facts.evidence: I was afraid of that.

facts.heading: Fear of being forced
facts.content: Tomas feared someone would force him to leave the door open and go.
facts.evidence: I thought someone would force me to leave the door open and go.

facts.heading: Small step is big
facts.content: Tomas stated that even checking the door once is big for him.
facts.evidence: But even that is big for me.

facts.heading: Telling Barbora he loves her
facts.content: Tomas wants to tell Barbora that he loves her.
facts.evidence: That I love her.

facts.heading: Need treatment to keep Barbora
facts.content: Tomas feels he needs to get treated so he doesn't lose Barbora.
facts.evidence: And that I need to get treated so I don't lose her.

facts.heading: Fear of Barbora's feelings
facts.content: Tomas is afraid that Barbora wouldn't want to be with him.
facts.evidence: Right now I'm afraid she wouldn't want to be with me.

facts.heading: Barbora's expected reaction
facts.content: Tomas believes Barbora would probably hug him.
facts.evidence: She would probably hug me.

facts.heading: Tomas can handle telling part
facts.content: Tomas stated he could handle telling Barbora at least part of what he learned.
facts.evidence: I could handle that.

facts.heading: Trial task for next session
facts.content: Tomas agreed to try checking the door once when leaving the apartment.
facts.evidence: Once. I'll try it.

facts.heading: Rating anxiety level
facts.content: Tomas agreed to write down a number from one to ten after checking the door.
facts.evidence: and I'll write down a number from one to ten.
